questions.explanation: Underwriting is the process used to determine entry into the group. Underwriting includes assessing the risk to determine the exposure of the group and determining the premium to be charged based on the risk.

title: Principles of Insurance — Test 4
description: IC-01 Practice Test 4 — Covers core principles, risk management, underwriting, reinsurance, and insurance concepts.

questions.question: Under which of the following circumstances, a fact is said to be material to the assessment of risk?
options: A fact is said to be material if it does not affect the decision of the underwriter to accept or reject the risk, or to determine the rates, terms and conditions if the risk is accepted
A fact is said to be material if the third-party, responsible for the accident is not absolved of his or her financial responsibility
A fact is said to be material, if it affects the decision of the underwriter to accept or reject the risk or to determine the rates, terms and conditions if the risk is accepted
A fact is said to be material if it does not involve more than one insurance policies drawn up on the same subject-matter and the insured cannot recover his or her loss from all the insurers
A fact is said to be material, if involves more than one insurance policies drawn up on the same subject-matter and the insured cannot recover his or her loss from all the insurers
questions.correctAnswer: A fact is said to be material, if it affects the decision of the underwriter to accept or reject the risk or to determine the rates, terms and conditions if the risk is accepted
questions.explanation: According to the principle of utmost good faith, the proposer is obliged to declare all relevant facts that are material to the assessment of the risk, at the time of making the proposal. A fact is said to be material, if it affects the decision of the underwriter to accept or reject the risk or to determine rates, terms and conditions if the risk is accepted.

questions.question: Full form of MLM is __________.
questions.explanation: Multi-level Marketing (MLM) or network marketing, is individuals selling products to the public - often by word of mouth and direct sales.

questions.question: Identify the correct statement from the following, with regards to a Free-Look-Period?
options: Discontinuing an existing policy and taking a new one for free
Choosing between two plans, one of which has considerably less premium or commission than the other
A prospective customer is allowed to look freely at the policy document within seven days and read it in depth
If a policy holder is not satisfied with the product, he or she can opt to return it to the insurance company within 15 days
Making a full and adequate disclosure of all the facts to allow the customers to make informed decisions
questions.correctAnswer: If a policy holder is not satisfied with the product, he or she can opt to return it to the insurance company within 15 days
questions.explanation: IRDA has prescribed a free look period of 15 days for life, general insurance and health policies. As per this stipulation, if a policy holder is not satisfied with the product, he/she can opt to return the same to the insurance company within a period of 15 days from the date of receipt of the document.

questions.question: Which of the following is evidence of an insurance contract?
questions.explanation: The insurance policy is the evidence of the contract and states the terms and conditions of the contract, details of promises made by the insurer, obligations of the policyholder and conditions attached thereto.

questions.question: Which of the following options is INCORRECT with regards to perils in fire insurance policies?
options: Perils relating to war-risks are excluded
Exclusions of perils are mentioned separately under the relevant section
Fire Insurance policies are 'Named Peril Policies', where the perils are listed
Perils such as impact of vehicles, riots, typhoons, cyclones, strike cannot be included
Add-on cover which are additional perils offered by the insurers may be opted for separately
questions.correctAnswer: Perils such as impact of vehicles, riots, typhoons, cyclones, strike cannot be included
questions.explanation: Fire insurance policies provide cover for financial losses due to damage to property arising out of fire, explosions etc. Fire policies may also cover damage through impact of vehicles, riots, typhoons, cyclones, strike or other malicious acts etc.

questions.question: In most cases, there is __________, when customers make purchases especially when purchasing tangible goods.
questions.explanation: When customers make purchases, especially when purchasing tangible goods, there is, in most cases an immediate sense of gratification or satisfaction from that purchase.

questions.question: Rahul single-handedly manages various departments and handles all the day to day activities of Rosewood Ltd. He is the ________ of Rosewood.
questions.explanation: A company has insurable interest in the life of certain important people whose absence can affect the company adversely. These people are key people and the company can take Keyman Insurance on the lives of these people.

questions.question: Identify from the following, the statement which is correct with respect to Valued-Policies.
options: Valued Policies are also known as Floater-Policies
Valued-Policies are also known as First-Loss Policies
Valued Policies are also known as Full-Value Policies
Valued Policies are also known as Declaration-Policies
Valued Policies are also known as Admitted-Value Polices
questions.correctAnswer: Valued Policies are also known as Admitted-Value Polices
questions.explanation: Valued policies are also called agreed value or admitted value policies, where the insurer agrees to pay a certain amount in the event of a total loss without taking into account allowances for depreciation or appreciation. This is not relevant for partial losses.

questions.question: Which of the following is a Contract?
options: Ram agrees with Shyam to kill Vishal for which Shyam agrees to pay Ram Rs. 10 Lakhs.
Renjit agrees to accompany Roshan for the weekend picnic.
Sudhir agrees to indemnify the loss in transit of smuggled goods of Shankar worth Rs. 10 Crores.
Rekha agrees to sell her house to Reshma for a consideration of Rs. 2 Crores.
questions.correctAnswer: Rekha agrees to sell her house to Reshma for a consideration of Rs. 2 Crores.
questions.explanation: Option 4 is considered as a contract as it is legally enforceable. All other options are not legally enforceable.

questions.question:
From the following data, calculate the Frequency of road accidents:
BRANCH | NUMBER OF THEFTS | NUMBER OF ACCIDENTS | NUMBER OF VEHICLES COVERED
A | 2 | 11 | 150
B | 3 | 19 | 160
C | 82 | 766 | 3600
D | 13 | 704 | 6090
questions.explanation: Total number of accidents = 11 + 19 + 766 + 704 = 1,500. Total number of vehicles covered = 150 + 160 + 3,600 + 6,090 = 10,000. Frequency = (Total accidents / Total vehicles) × 100 = (1,500 / 10,000) × 100 = 15%.

questions.question: When the Underwriter drafts the terms for the Policy for a risk underwritten, which function does he perform?
questions.explanation: Drafting the terms of cover is part of the Acceptance process.

questions.question: Which of the following Acts deals with Directors' Liability?
questions.explanation: The Companies Act, 2013 has significant provisions on liability of the Directors which are important for coverage under Directors and Officers Liability Insurance.

questions.question: What is Commoditisation?
options: Lack of distinction between different competing products
Pricing very competitively even by incurring losses
Pricing very high by creating a brand value
questions.correctAnswer: Lack of distinction between different competing products
questions.explanation: Commoditisation is lack of distinction between different competing products because Commoditisation treats every product as a commodity, and obscures distinctive feature of each product.

questions.question: A priori means __________.
options: Knowledge considered to be true without being based on previous experience
questions.correctAnswer: Knowledge considered to be true without being based on previous experience
questions.explanation: Knowledge considered to be true without being based on previous experience is known as a priori. You need not conduct an experiment to calculate the probability of getting a head in a toss of a coin. You know it a priori.

questions.question: Which of the following does not have an Insurable Interest?
options: Bailee's responsibility for goods entrusted to him.
Proposer's interest in the life of his friend.
Contractor on the building being constructed by him.
questions.correctAnswer: Proposer's interest in the life of his friend.
questions.explanation: While all the other three circumstances entail an Insurable Interest, no person is deemed to have an Insurable Interest in the life of a friend.

questions.question: Raju had a Health Insurance Policy for Rs.3,00,000. His Policy had a Co Pay of 20%. He was admitted to a Hospital for an Illness, and spent Rs.60,000. How much would he get from his Insurer?
questions.explanation: On the amount of loss of Rs.60,000, a 20% Co Pay is to be deducted which is Rs.12,000 (20% of 60,000). Hence (60,000 - 12,000) i.e. only Rs.48,000 is payable.

questions.question: A risk with a Sum Insured of Rs. 600 Crores is ceded to a Reinsurer under a Five Line Surplus Treaty. The Insurer's Retention is Rs. 100 Crores. If the loss is for Rs. 60 Crores, how much would the Reinsurer pay?
questions.explanation: Since the loss amount (Rs. 60 Crores) is less than the Insurer's Retention (Rs. 100 Crores), the Reinsurer would not pay anything in this scenario.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a Non-Proportional Reinsurance?
questions.explanation: Surplus is a Proportional Reinsurance arrangement.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Probability of future losses is better estimated if the number of records of past losses is higher
The longer the period over which the data is Studied, the more effective would be the estimated probability of future events
Losses from emerging risks cannot be accurately predicted
The estimated probability will be effective even if the number of risks underwritten is low
questions.correctAnswer: The estimated probability will be effective even if the number of risks underwritten is low
questions.explanation: Even if the exercise of estimating future loss probabilities is properly carried out, with a large volume of records, over a long period of time, if the number of risks underwritten, based on such estimates, is less, the difference between actual outcome and expected outcome could be significant. The Law will work only when sufficiently large number of risks is underwritten.

questions.question: What is meant by Concurrent causes?
options: In All Risk Policies, where the cause could not be identified.
Two or more Perils occurring at the same time
Caused by Electric Short circuit and resulting in Fire.
Different Causes occurring independent of each other.
questions.correctAnswer: Two or more Perils occurring at the same time
questions.explanation: Some times two causes could be happening together, not necessarily one after the other, but simultaneously. Such simultaneous causes are called concurrent causes.

questions.question: If the Direct Claims Paid for the Current Year is Rs.12000 Crores, the Reserve for Outstanding Claims at the end of the Current Year is Rs.18000 Crores, and the Reserve for Outstanding Claims at the end of the Previous Year is Rs.16000 Crores, what is the Gross Incurred Claims for the Current Year?
questions.explanation: Gross Incurred Claims for the Current Year = Direct Claims Paid + Reserve for Outstanding Claims at the end of the Current Year - Reserve for Outstanding Claims at the end of the Previous Year = 12000 + 18000 - 16000 = Rs.14000 Crores.

questions.question: Proper Underwriting enables __________.
questions.explanation: A proper Underwriting would mean that the pool of the risks underwritten would be very similar to the pool of risks the Actuary had based her workings on. Proper Underwriting thus enables better loss prediction.

questions.question: The Statement of Assets and Liabilities of a Company as at the end of the financial year is called:
questions.explanation: The Statement of Assets and Liabilities of a Company as at the end of the financial year is called Balance Sheet.

questions.question: Identify the statement that is TRUE. Insurers agree to__________.
questions.explanation: Insurance is a contract that compensates the financial loss suffered by the Insured caused by an insured peril. The Insurers pay more than the premium received, because they collect premium money from various persons who are exposed to the same kind of risk, but not all people facing the same risk suffer losses.

questions.question: It is not feasible for the insurer to inspect each and every risk proposed for insurance as __________.
options: the insurer's information system is not designed for risk inspection
the insurer does not have knowledge of the risk
the policy carries the condition of Utmost Good Faith
the insurer is not interested in knowing about the risk
the number of risks proposed for insurance are many and it would not be feasible
questions.correctAnswer: the number of risks proposed for insurance are many and it would not be feasible
questions.explanation: An insurer receives hundreds of proposals from the public to cover their risks. It is also not feasible for the insurer to inspect each and every risk before accepting it for insurance. The customer who makes the proposal is expected to have intimate knowledge on the features of the risk proposed to be insured. The insurer, therefore, trusts the insured customer to disclose all facts material to the risk being proposed for insurance.

questions.question: Why is mysterious disappearance not covered?
options: Since reason of loss cannot be ascertained
Since it takes place very often
Since the amount of loss cannot be ascertained
questions.correctAnswer: Since reason of loss cannot be ascertained
questions.explanation: Some of the insurance policies cover only certain named Perils. Some policies cover All Risks, but even such All Risks policies exclude losses caused by a number of Perils. Hence, in order to determine admissibility, the insurer should know the cause of loss. That is why losses like mysterious disappearances are not covered.

questions.question: The insurer __________ in Liability Claims.
options: pays the insured only when he is held not liable
pays the insured after he fulfills the court order
pays the insured even though he does not fulfill the court order
deposits the money with the victim
makes payment only if the insured is not at fault
questions.correctAnswer: pays the insured after he fulfills the court order
questions.explanation: In liability insurance, the insurer typically indemnifies (compensates) the insured only after the insured has satisfied the court order or paid the claim to the third party (the victim). This ensures that the insured fulfils their legal obligations, and the insurer then reimburses the insured for the loss, as per the terms of the policy.

questions.question: Explain the relation between Burning cost and Premium.
options: Burning cost minus other cost elements
Burning cost loaded with other cost elements
questions.correctAnswer: Burning cost loaded with other cost elements
questions.explanation: Burning cost represents the historical claims experience for a particular risk and is used to estimate the premium required to cover expected future losses. In premium calculation, burning cost serves as the foundation, but additional cost elements such as operating expenses, commissions, profit margin, and risk adjustments are added to determine the final premium charged to policyholders.

questions.question: Reserve for IBNR is created when claim has occurred __________.
options: and has been reported in current year but not paid
and has been reported and also paid in the current year
in current year but has not been reported
and has been reported in previous year but paid in current year
and has been reported and paid in the previous year
questions.correctAnswer: in current year but has not been reported
questions.explanation: IBNR stands for 'Incurred But Not Reported.' It refers to claims that have already occurred (the insured event has taken place) by the end of an accounting period, but the insurance company has not yet received a claim report for them. This reserve ensures that insurers are financially prepared to handle such unknown liabilities.

questions.question: Choose the risks that a Risk manager should identify.
questions.explanation: Risk Management is initially concerned with identifying risks. An enterprise faces various risks. Some of them are from Pure Risks, some from Speculative Risks. It is the duty of Risk Management to identify all risks the enterprise is exposed to.

questions.question: Identify the statement that is NOT TRUE.
options: Insurers provide compensation for sentimental losses
Insurers agree to make good losses
Insurers provide compensation for financial losses
Insurers make payment only if losses arise out of an insured peril
Insurers make payment only if the insured has suffered a loss
questions.correctAnswer: Insurers provide compensation for sentimental losses
questions.explanation: Insurance is a loss sharing mechanism. Insurance is a contract that compensates the financial loss suffered by the Insured caused by an insured peril. Losses caused by uninsured or excluded Perils are not covered by insurance. Insurers do not compensate sentimental losses.

questions.question: Identify the unique feature of Proportional Treaties.
options: Just the premium is shared proportionately
There is equal sharing of risk
There is proportionate sharing of premium
There is equal sharing of loss
There is proportionate sharing of risk, premium and loss
questions.correctAnswer: There is proportionate sharing of risk, premium and loss
questions.explanation: The most striking feature of Proportional Treaties is that risks, premium and losses are shared between the Insurer and Reinsurer in some proportion. Non-Proportional Treaties, in contrast, do not share risks, premium and losses in any proportion.

questions.question: Hazard study is required to __________.
questions.explanation: A hazard study is typically conducted to identify and understand hazards in a given environment, process, or system. This helps in assessing potential risks and preventing accidents or losses. Hazard studies are crucial for safety management and risk mitigation strategies.

questions.question: Calculate the premium, when the burning cost is given as 1000, fixed cost is 200 and the other cost is 30%.
questions.explanation: Premium = (Burning Cost + Fixed Costs) / (1 - Other Costs) = (1000 + 200) / (1 - 0.30) = 1200 / 0.70 = Rs. 1714.29.

questions.question: Which of the following is considered to be the best measure for efficacy of underwriting?
questions.explanation: The efficacy of the Underwriting System should be periodically evaluated. Efficacy of Underwriting depends on how closely the accepted pool of risks matches the expected pool of risks. This is best measured by the loss ratios for the pool.

questions.question:
Identify the statement that is CORRECT.
Statement a: All perils are covered by some policies without exception
Statement b: All perils are not covered by All Risk Policies
options: a is correct in case b is correct
questions.explanation: In the insurance world, there is no Policy which covers all kinds of Perils. Even coverage under All Risks Policy does not cover all Perils. Therefore, in any Insurance, there are some Perils which are covered, there are some Perils which are not covered, and some Perils which are specifically excluded.

questions.question: Identify the statement that is TRUE
options: All speculative risks could lead to a loss
Pure risks could lead to profit or loss
Speculative risks could lead to profit or loss
All pure risks could lead to profit
All pure risks are speculative risks
questions.correctAnswer: Speculative risks could lead to profit or loss
questions.explanation: Risks could be grouped into Pure Risks and Speculative Risks. Speculative Risks could result in three possible outcomes: Profit, Loss and No Profit No Loss. Pure Risks are those that cause a loss, with no possibility of a gain.

questions.question: __________ premium is taken into account to calculate the profit of the company.
questions.explanation: Once the Net Earned Premium, Net Incurred Claims, Net Commission, Operating Expenses and Investment Income are calculated, Net Profit of the Company is worked out.

questions.question: If the insurer sells the salvage before settling the loss and receives the money for the sale, what will be the consequence?
options: The full amount of the loss is paid by the insurer and he also makes payment for salvage proceeds to the insured
The full amount of the loss is paid by the insurer without deducting for salvage
Payment for the claim is made by the insurer even though the claim is not admissible
Salvage proceeds are deducted by the insurer and balance amount is settled with the insured
The claim is denied by the insurer even if it is admissible
questions.correctAnswer: Salvage proceeds are deducted by the insurer and balance amount is settled with the insured
questions.explanation: In insurance claims involving property damage, if the insurer sells the salvage before settling the claim, they recover some money from it. To avoid overcompensation to the insured (which violates the principle of indemnity), the salvage value is deducted from the total claim amount. The insurer then pays only the net loss to the insured.

questions.question: __________ is not considered to be an example of Avoidance.
options: Not building the factory in an area which is earthquake prone
Not building the factory near a river
questions.explanation: Certain losses could be prevented by adopting safety measures like wearing helmets which is an example of Risk Mitigation, not Risk Avoidance. Not storing or manufacturing hazardous goods, not building in earthquake-prone areas, and not building near a river are all examples of Risk Avoidance.

questions.question:
Identify which of these two statements is TRUE.
A) If there is no deviation from the expected outcome, there is no risk
B) If there is no expectation, there is no risk
questions.explanation: Risk is the possibility of a deviation from an expected outcome. There is no risk that the sun will not rise in the east tomorrow — it unfailingly rises in the east, so there is no deviation and no risk. But not all things are as sure as the sunrise. If there is no expectation, there can be no risk.

questions.question: Salvage means __________.
questions.explanation: In a property loss, some amount could be saved from the damage. This amount depends on the nature of property insured, and the cause and extent of loss. In most cases, some value is recoverable as scrap. The value that could be recovered from the damaged property is called salvage. When a claim is settled, the salvage value is reduced from the amount payable.

questions.question: The underwriter should study __________ while analysing a risk.
options: perils covered and hazards involved therein
questions.correctAnswer: perils covered and hazards involved therein
questions.explanation: The task that the Insurer should undertake before deciding on whether to accept a risk or to decline a risk, is to first evaluate the risk. Evaluation begins with collection of information on the risk and its features. The information collected would help the Insurer understand the nature of risk, the context of its exposure, the Perils to be covered, and the hazards to which the risk is exposed.

questions.question: A balanced book involves __________.
questions.explanation: While every Insurer would like to write more and more of the same type of risk, concentration of business in one line, one region, one channel, one group of clients could seriously impair the Company's performance. A balanced book is one with diversified business from various geographies, clients, channels and products.

questions.question: Uberrimae Fidei is a __________ phrase.
questions.explanation: Insurance contracts are contracts of utmost good faith. The parties to the contract have a duty to disclose all material facts even without being asked. This is called the Duty of Disclosure. Uberrimae fidei is a Latin phrase, meaning Utmost Good Faith.

questions.question: What is meant by Loss development factor?
options: Development of aggregate liability during claims cycle
Study of underwriting to lower the loss
Development of profits during the period of loss
Hazard study to see how losses occur
questions.correctAnswer: Development of aggregate liability during claims cycle
questions.explanation: Determining the rates for different products is a very complex exercise. One of the factors to be considered is the Loss Development factor — the manner of development of aggregate liability over the claim maturity cycle.

questions.question: Identify the incorrect statement.
options: Profit is not included in price
Number of losses per number of exposure units constitutes frequency
Units of risk constitute exposure unit
Severity means average of the losses
Frequency multiplied by severity equals to burning cost
questions.correctAnswer: Profit is not included in price
questions.explanation: In insurance, price (premium) includes: Burning cost (expected claims), Expenses, Profit margin, and Contingencies. So, profit is indeed included in the insurance price to ensure the insurer's financial sustainability. Therefore, the incorrect statement is 'Profit is not included in price'.

questions.question: Identify the peril not applicable to a property.
questions.explanation: A peril refers to a specific cause of loss or damage to property, such as: Flood, Earthquake, Fire, Storm. All of the above are physical perils that can directly damage property. Liability is not a peril, but a type of insurance coverage that protects against legal responsibility for injury or damage to others.

questions.question: In India, the insurer has to be a Corporation or a Company incorporated under the ________.
questions.explanation: In India, insurers are required to be incorporated as a company under the Companies Act or be established as a corporation under a specific Act of Parliament.

questions.question: Which Indian act lays down the conditions of a valid contract and the when it becomes voidable, how it can be revoked etc.?
questions.explanation: The Indian Contract Act lays down the conditions of a valid contract, when it becomes voidable, and how it can be revoked. It forms the legal basis for all contracts in India, including insurance contracts.

title: Principles of Insurance — Test 5
description: IC-01 Last Day Revision Test 2 — 100 questions covering all core insurance principles.

questions.question: Select from below the correct option, for which group insurance policies cannot be issued.
options: Banks for their loan account holders
questions.explanation: Group policies can be issued to employers representing companies/organisations, professional associations representing a group, trade unions, banks for their loan accountholders, and any other professional organisation representing a group of people brought together for a common objective. A sole proprietor carrying on business is not a group.

questions.question: The events such as earthquakes or tsunamis can put a strain on the funds of the insurer. This happens because __________.
options: there would be economic downturn following such events
weather patterns become unreliable after such events
government does not offer enough assistance packages following such events
there would be thousands of claims amounting to extremely large sums of money
government doles out the assistance packages following such events
questions.correctAnswer: there would be thousands of claims amounting to extremely large sums of money
questions.explanation: Insurers normally have enough funds to pay claims, however, events such as earthquakes or tsunamis can put a strain on the funds of the insurer as there would be thousands of claims amounting to extremely large sums of money.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is not true with respect to the Insurance Institute of India?
options: The College of Insurance in Mumbai was established in 1966 as the training wing of the Insurance Institute of India.
Over the last 50 years the Insurance Institute of India has gained recognition as a premier institute for education in this part of the world.
The Insurance Institute of India conducts examinations and offers Licentiate Certificate, Associateship Diploma and Fellowship Diploma.
Insurance Institute of India conducts examinations in 19 centres, all of which are situated in India.
The Federation of Insurance Institutes was the original name of the institute which was set up in Mumbai to cater the needs of students in India.
questions.correctAnswer: Insurance Institute of India conducts examinations in 19 centres, all of which are situated in India.
questions.explanation: The Insurance Institute of India conducts examinations in 19 centres in Asia, Africa and Fiji — not all of which are situated in India.

questions.question: What is the full form of PML?
questions.explanation: The total loss that can happen is referred to as the Maximum Possible Loss (MPL). The risk exposure is the MPL multiplied by the probability of the peril striking. This is called the Probable Maximum Loss (PML). MPL x Probability of Peril Striking = Probable Maximum Loss (PML).

questions.question: Which of the following pair is together called as Ethics in Business?
questions.explanation: There has been increased discussion about accountability and corporate governance, which together are called Ethics in Business.

questions.question: Explain the term Representation.
options: Any amendments to the standard policy conditions.
The evidence of the contract which states the norms and conditions of the contract, details of the promises made by the insurer and the conditions attached they're off.
The amount of money or commission that has to be paid in exchange for the insurance.
A statement which has a bearing on the risk, regardless of whether made in writing of verbal, by the person requesting insurance.
A contractual process where in a person protect their physical assets as well as life from certain events or perils by transferring the risk.

questions.question: Identify from the following, the fund which is not a variant of the basic funds offered by insurance companies under the Unit Linked Insurance Plan (ULIP) in India.

questions.question: If the occurrence of an event at a given point of time and its impact are certain then the insurance company __________.
options: has to compulsorily cover such events
is bound by law to cover at least but not limited to 50% of such events
is bound by law to cover at least but not limited to 25% of such events
is bound by law to cover at least but not limited to 90% of such events
questions.explanation: If the occurrence of an event at a given point of time and its impact are certain then the insurance company may not cover such events. In short, insurance means 'loss of a few shared by many'.

questions.question: Complete the following statement: "Health insurance claims are now being serviced by a network of Third-Party Administrators (TPA) who have been licensed by __________."
questions.explanation: Health insurance claims are now being serviced by a network of Third Party Administrators (TPA) who have been licensed by IRDA. TPAs tie up with hospitals across the country and include them in their network.

questions.question: How can you differentiate between Principle of Indemnity and the Principle of Utmost Good Faith?
options: Indemnity is where insurance places the insured in the same financial position after the loss as they enjoyed before it; not better, whereas Utmost Good Faith is where a duty of disclosure is imposed on both the insurer and insured to disclose all material facts relevant to the insurance contract.

Utmost Good Faith is when a person said to stand to gain from the continued existence of the person of property insured and would suffer a financial loss if there is a damage to the person or property, whereas indemnity is where more than one insurance policies drawn up on the same subject matter and the insured cannot recover his loss from all the insurers.

Utmost Good Faith is where insurance places the insured in the same financial position after the loss as they enjoyed before if not better, whereas indemnity is where duty of disclosure is imposed on both the insurer and the insured to disclose all material facts relevant to the insurance contract.

questions.question: Judge whether the following statement is correct or not. "A husband can take life insurance cover but not the health insurance cover for his wife and vice versa."
options: Incorrect – A husband can take life assurance, but not health insurance cover for his wife and vice versa
Incorrect - A wife can take Life assurance cover but not health insurance cover for a husband and vice versa

Incorrect – A husband can take life insurance cover and / or health insurance cover for his wife and vice versa
questions.correctAnswer: Incorrect – A husband can take life insurance cover and / or health insurance cover for his wife and vice versa
questions.explanation: A husband has insurable interest in the life of his wife and similarly, the wife has insurable interest in the life of the husband. Both benefit from the well-being of each other and if something goes wrong with any one of them it affects the other adversely. So, the husband can take life insurance cover and/or health insurance cover for his wife and vice versa.

questions.question: The combined figure of loss ratio plus expense ratio is called the __________ and this figure reflects the overall underwriting profitability.
questions.explanation: The combined figure of loss ratio plus expense ratio is called the combined ratio and this figure reflects the overall underwriting profitability.

questions.question: How can you define an insurance broker?
options: An insurance broker is an individual, a company, a society, or a firm, wholly engaged in sourcing insurance business for various insurance companies.

An insurance broker is an institution established by the act of Parliament.

questions.explanation: An insurance broker is an individual, a company, a society or a firm, wholly engaged in sourcing insurance business for various insurance companies.

questions.question: When does the real value of life assurance is experienced?
questions.explanation: In the case of life insurance, the customer who buys the policy may not be the same customer who is making a claim on the policy. The real value of life insurance is experienced at the time of claim.

questions.question: Choose the correct option and complete the sentence. Healthcare policies exclude treatment of pre-existing diseases or diseases contracted within __________ days of commencement of policies.
questions.explanation: Healthcare policies also exclude treatment for diseases prevalent at the time of taking the policy for the first time known as 'pre-existing diseases' or contracted within 30 days of such commencement. In the Indian market, companies cover pre-existing diseases after a continuous cover for a period of 48 months.

questions.question: Strict limits are placed on insurers by law and regulation limiting the__________.
options: Amount they can invest in gold bonds
Amount they can invest in any one company
Numbers of products by insurance company
Claims paid out to the companies
questions.correctAnswer: Amount they can invest in any one company
questions.explanation: Insurers also invest in Indian companies, by giving them loans and subscribing to their shares. Share of insurers in the capital of companies, both equity and debt together, would not be 20% or more.

questions.question: __________ is called as the 'Life Fund' in life assurance.
questions.explanation: When an insurer receives premium, a certain amount is set aside to meet their liabilities. This is called premium reserve. In life insurance, premium reserve is called the life fund. All revenues go into the life fund and all claims are met out of the life fund.

questions.question: In which year the Foreign Direct Investment was allowed in insurance?
questions.explanation: In the year 2000, the insurance sector was liberalised and opened up for business to the private sector. Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) was allowed in insurance up to 26% wherein the foreign players were allowed to enter into joint ventures with domestic players.

questions.question: Identify from below, the correct name of the health insurance policy which caters to the medical needs of a family.
questions.explanation: Family Floater Policy: This type of health insurance policy caters to the medical needs of a family. In family floater policies, normally insurance companies allow coverage for up to two adults and two children in a family. The sum insured can be shared by the family members covered in the policy.

questions.question: Study the below options with regards to Principle of Subrogation and Principle of Contribution and select the correct option which proves the given statement wrong: "Principle of subrogation and the principle of contribution do not apply to_________."
questions.explanation: The principles of subrogation and contribution do not apply to life insurance policies or personal accident policies. This is because loss of life and human suffering can never be fully assessed or compensated. The principles of subrogation and contribution apply only to contracts of indemnity.

questions.question: Identify from the following the fund which is not a variant of the basic funds offered by insurance companies, under the Unit Linked Insurance Plan (ULIP).
questions.explanation: Money market funds invest in high quality, short-term debt securities and pay dividends that generally reflect short-term interest rates. They do not invest in equity like ULIPs. Insurance companies have different names for these funds e.g., Growth Fund, Balanced Fund, Protector Fund, Preserver Fund, Maximiser, Multiplier, Gilt Fund, Enhancer, Dynamic Fund, Sectoral Fund, Conservative Fund, Growth Super, Builder, Value Fund etc.

questions.question: Identify which one of the following are named Peril policies.
options: Named peril policies are the policies where non-financial losses in general are covered.
Named peril policies are the policies where the batteries are listed.
Named peril policies are the policies where non-financial losses due to various bills are covered.
Named peril policies are the policies where non-financial losses due to loss of life are covered
questions.explanation: Fire policies are 'named peril policies' where the perils are listed. Exclusions are mentioned separately under the relevant section. Add on covers which are additional perils offered by the insurers, may be opted for separately. Example - earthquake cover.

questions.question: Choose the correct option from the following with regards to Insurance Contract.
options: The insurance company agrees to pay the policyholder a certain sum of money, provided the policyholder has been paying the premium(s) as specified in the insurance contract.
The insurance company agrees to pay the policyholder some part of the sum assured, even if the policyholder has been paying the premium.

The policy holder agrees to pay to the insurance company a certain sum of money, if the insured event occurs, provided premiums have been paid.
None of the above is correct
questions.correctAnswer: The insurance company agrees to pay the policyholder a certain sum of money, provided the policyholder has been paying the premium(s) as specified in the insurance contract.
questions.explanation: According to the insurance contract: The insurance company agrees to pay the policyholder a certain sum of money (sum assured); If the event (death or peril e.g., fire, earthquake etc.) specified in the insurance contract happens; Provided the policyholder has been paying the premium(s) as specified in the insurance contract.

questions.question: Define the term Retrocession.
options: Retrocession means when the insurer accepts the business from individual

Retrocession means when the reinsurer accepts the business from an individual
Retrocession means when a reinsurer reinsures with another reinsurer or insurance company

questions.explanation: A reinsurer reinsures with another reinsurer or insurance company. Such process of transfer is called 'retrocession'.

questions.question: Identify from below the correct statement with regards to 'Insurance'.
options: Insurance is mainly created to reduce the taxation effects
All insurance policies are based on the number of people availing the insurance
All insurance policies are based on the number of people who are in debt at any given point of time
Insurance is a mechanism that helps to reduce the financial effects of adverse situations
questions.correctAnswer: Insurance is a mechanism that helps to reduce the financial effects of adverse situations
questions.explanation: Insurance is a mechanism by which the economic losses that one would suffer as a result of an event can be shared by all the members of a group. Insurance is a mechanism that helps to reduce the financial effects of adverse situations.

questions.question: Choose from below the kind of risks that are preferred by insurers.
options: Risks that are 100% higher than the standard risks
Risks that are 10% higher than the standard risks
Risks that are 20% higher than the standard risks
Risks that are significantly higher than the standard risks
Risks that are significantly lower than the standard risks
questions.correctAnswer: Risks that are significantly lower than the standard risks
questions.explanation: Risks that are significantly lower than the standard risks are preferred by insurers.

questions.question: Identify from below the incorrect statement with regards to insurance brokers.

questions.question: Verify the following statement: 'The Insurance Act has strict guidelines for insurance companies about investing money.'
options: To ensure that the premium selected are invested only in risk-free investments, returns being not a concern for the insurance company.

questions.question: Identify the statement if it is True or False: 'The fees payable for the licence varies according to the category and also whether the surveyor is an individual or a company / firm.'

questions.question: Which risk is associated with changes in consumer preferences?
questions.explanation: Dynamic risks are those resulting from changes in the economy. Changes in the price level, consumer tastes, fashions, income and output, technology, political upheavals or Government suddenly losing vote of confidence may cause financial loss to the members of the economy.

questions.question: Identify the incorrect statement from the following with respect to electronically held insurance policies and paper policies.

There is no risk of loss or damage of a policy, as it is common with paper policies as the electronic form ensures that the policies are in safe custody and can be easily accessed whenever and wherever needed.

questions.explanation: An E-insurance Account or Electronic Insurance Account or eIA is like a depository to keep your insurance policies in the electronic mode. It saves you from unnecessary paperwork, and safeguards in case you lose your policies.

questions.question: Under Frequency of annuities in Annuity Contracts, the plans offered by insurance companies give the annuitant the option to receive the annuity payments. Identify which of the following periods cannot be opted by the annuitant.
questions.explanation: Under Frequency of annuities in Annuity Contracts, the plans offered by insurance companies give the annuitant the option to receive the annuity payments monthly, quarterly, half-yearly or annually.

questions.question: The insurer uses his past experience to estimate what will happen in the future, however, due to __________ the future will not be similar to the past.

questions.explanation: The insurer uses his past experience to estimate what will happen in the future. However, due to climate change and changes in technology and industry the future will not be similar to the past.

questions.question: Sunder bought a general insurance policy for his factory the period of one year. Can he renew the same insurance policy at the end of one year?

questions.question: Choose from the following, the most appropriate premium paying option offered by Life Insurance Companies to the policy holders.
options: As a single premium through Electronic Clearing Services (ECS)

Principle of Contribution; Principle of Liability

Principle of Subrogation; Principle of Contribution

questions.question: Fill in the blanks with correct option: The Sum-Assured is the ______ amount of the insurer's liability under the policy.

questions.question: The commission rate ______ with the kind of business, for general insurance business.
questions.explanation: For general insurance business, the contract is usually for a period of twelve months and the commission rate varies with the kind of business.

questions.question: By profession, Mohit is an engineer working as a production manager but he also works as a pizza delivery man after his regular job. Referring to the scenario, which of the following insurance policies should Mohit opt for?
questions.explanation: Personal Accident policies cover death or disablement arising out of accidents of any kind (caused by external, violent and visible means). In the case of personal accident policies, there is no need for assessment of risk, except on the factor of occupation.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding application of indemnity in the case of liability insurance?

Liability policies are issued, where the declared value represents the manufacture's production price of the ship
questions.correctAnswer: Liability policies indemnify the insured in respect of damages, awarded by the law for personal injuries or damage to property of third-parties.
questions.explanation: Liability policies (motor third party, public liability, products liability etc.) indemnify the insured in respect of damages awarded by law for personal injuries or damage to property of third parties.

questions.question: There is no current __________ for the insurance customer; it is imaginary at the time of purchase.
questions.explanation: The customer has to visualise the possibility of a tragedy before they seek insurance. There is no current discomfort for the insurance customer; it is imaginary at the time of purchase, and it is the insurance salesperson's job to create those unpleasant images for the customer.

questions.question: Complete the following statement with correct option: Treaties may specify that re-insurance would be a certain proportion of the risk __________.
questions.explanation: Reinsurance is not a simple business; it is complex and can be arranged in numerous ways. Treaties may specify that reinsurance would be a certain proportion of the risk underwritten by the insurance company.

questions.question: Tara Hotels has taken insurance with Gemini Insurance Company for their restaurant premises. False: A husband can take life assurance cover but not health insurance cover for his wife and not the other way round.
questions.correctAnswer: False: A husband can take life assurance cover and/or health insurance cover for his wife and vice versa
questions.explanation: A husband has an insurable interest in the life of his wife and similarly, the wife has insurable interest in the life of the husband. Both benefit from the well-being of each other and if something goes wrong with any one of them it affects the other adversely. So, the husband can take life insurance cover and/or health insurance cover for his wife and vice versa.

questions.question: The basic cover under fire insurance may be extended to cover __________.
options: Deterioration of stocks in refrigerated ware-houses, due to power failure
questions.explanation: Fire insurance policies provide cover for financial losses due to damage to property arising out of fire, explosions etc. The basic cover may be extended to cover things like: professional fees for architect and consulting engineer, deterioration of stocks in refrigerated warehouses due to power failure, leakage and contamination, loss of rent, start-up expenses.

questions.question: Identify from the following, the option that correctly defines the average mind-set of person receiving the death claim.
options: A person who feels in- different
A person who regrets that he or she did not put his or her money to better use.
A person who doubts the wisdom of his or her choice of buying the policy
A person who wished he or she had spent the premium- money on other things that would provide more immediate enjoyment
A person who is feeling relieved from an anxiety, knowing he or she is receiving the money.
questions.correctAnswer: A person who is feeling relieved from an anxiety, knowing he or she is receiving the money.
questions.explanation: In the case of life insurance, the customer who buys the policy may not be the same customer who is making a claim on the policy. The real value of life insurance is experienced at the time of claim. The person who receives the death claim is the person who will also be feeling relieved from anxiety, knowing they are receiving the money.

questions.question: Why do insurance companies have individuals qualified in various disciplines and technologies on their panels?
options: Insurance companies have persons qualified in various disciplines and technologies on their panels so that their services can be called upon, to assess the loss and recommend the extent of claim payable in a particular case.

Insurance companies have persons qualified in various disciplines and technologies on their panels so that their services can be called upon, to advise the client on the various policies available and help them to choose a policy suitable for them.

Insurance companies have persons qualified in various disciplines and technologies on their panels so that their services can be called upon, to counsel the client to deal with the loss and file the claim.

Insurance companies have persons qualified in various disciplines and technologies on their panels so that their services can be called upon to advise the claims manager on how to calculate the claim payable in a particular case.

Insurance companies have persons qualified in various disciplines and technologies on their panels so that their service can be called upon to advise the insurance company to design new and innovative policies.
questions.correctAnswer: Insurance companies have persons qualified in various disciplines and technologies on their panels so that their services can be called upon, to assess the loss and recommend the extent of claim payable in a particular case.
questions.explanation: Non-life insurance covers a variety of risks. Many of them, due to their complicated nature, can be apprised only by technically competent persons. Insurers may not have technically competent persons in their offices for this. So, they have, in their panel, persons qualified in various disciplines and technologies, whose services can be called upon to assess the loss and recommend the extent of claim payable in a particular case.

questions.question: What is the purpose of servicing activities in the insurance industry?
options: Servicing activities encourage customers to leave things to fate
Servicing activities help defer the customer decision to buy insurance
Servicing activities involve understanding the customer mindset
Servicing activities ensure immediate customer satisfaction upon paying premiums
Servicing activities aim to retain customers and make sure that the customer is not attracted to another insurance company
questions.correctAnswer: Servicing activities aim to retain customers and make sure that the customer is not attracted to another insurance company
questions.explanation: The role of intermediaries is to keep the customers satisfied. Agents and brokers also are responsible to make sure that the customer is satisfied, when policies are taken. Servicing activities make sure that the customer is not attracted to another insurance company.

questions.question: Dynamic risks are those risks which __________.
options: are resulting from changes in the economy
can be measured or quantified in monetary terms
cannot be measured or quantified in monetary terms
questions.correctAnswer: are resulting from changes in the economy
questions.explanation: Dynamic risks are those resulting from changes in the economy. Changes in the price level, consumer tastes, fashions, income and output, technology, political upheavals or Government suddenly losing vote of confidence may cause financial loss to the members of the economy.

questions.question: General insurance contributes to the continuation of trade by __________.
options: setting the strict limits on payment of premiums
ensuring a proper flow of income in the economy
fulfilling the obligations at the claim time which in turn can prevent the business from going broke
by enabling the traders to register for the special offers
by setting the strict limits on the claims, that can be availed
questions.correctAnswer: fulfilling the obligations at the claim time which in turn can prevent the business from going broke
questions.explanation: General insurance contributes to the continuation of trade by fulfilling obligations at claim time which in turn can prevent businesses from going broke. Insurers work with loss prevention agencies in ports, docks and cargo depots by providing information on causes of losses.

questions.question: What is the term used when the life-assured transfers their existing investments from one fund to another during the tenure of the policy?
questions.explanation: The life insured can transfer their existing investments from one fund to another during the tenure of the policy. This process is known as 'Switching'.

questions.question: What is the fixed commission structure with regards to remuneration of insurance agents?
options: It is certain percentage of the profit paid by the insured
It is certain percentage of commission paid by the insurer
It is certain percentage of the salary paid by the insured
It is certain percentage of the premium paid by the insured
It is certain percentage of the professional charges paid by the insured
questions.correctAnswer: It is certain percentage of the premium paid by the insured
questions.explanation: Agents are remunerated by way of commissions, which are regulated by IRDA. Most of the products have a fixed commission structure which is a certain percentage of the premium paid by the insured.

questions.question: Which of the following risks is not covered by Fidelity Guarantee?
options: Risks related to loss of cash and securities
Compensation that is to be paid by the employee, for death
questions.correctAnswer: Compensation that is to be paid by the employee, for death
questions.explanation: Fidelity Guarantee covers risks related to dishonesty, fraud and embezzlement by employees etc. and protects employers from loss of cash and securities.

questions.question: Identify the features that increased the probability of loss.
questions.explanation: The Insurer is in the business of compensating losses. He analyses the Perils that a risk is exposed to, and chooses to cover only those losses which are caused by Specified Perils. The features that increase the probability of loss, and increase the amount of loss, are called Hazards.

questions.question: __________ is not an exposure unit.
questions.explanation: An Exposure Unit is the item, person, or object that is insured and used as the basis for calculating the premium and measuring the loss experience. Claims are the losses that occur — they are the result of the exposure unit suffering a peril, not the unit of exposure itself.

questions.question: What is the maximum amount payable under a policy?
options: The loss amount or sum that is insured whichever is lower
The loss amount or sum that is insured whichever is higher
questions.explanation: Almost all insurance policies specify the maximum amount of claim that is recoverable under the Policy. This amount is called the Sum Insured. No matter what the amount of loss is, if it exceeds the Sum Insured, the maximum amount payable is restricted to the Sum Insured.

questions.question: A 30% Quota share treaty covers all risks up to Rs.700 crores. In a risk for Rs.900 crores, in case of a loss of Rs.90 crores, calculate the amount that the treaty reinsurer would pay.
questions.explanation: Given: Quota Share Treaty = 30%, Treaty covers risks up to Rs.700 crores, Actual risk = Rs.900 crores, Loss = Rs.90 crores. Since the treaty limit is Rs.700 crores but the risk is Rs.900 crores, the treaty applies only proportionately. Eligible portion = 700/900 x 7/9. Treaty share = 30% of that eligible portion. So, reinsurer's effective share = 30% x 7/9 = 0.3 x 7/9 = 2.1/9 = 0.2333 (~23.33%). Applying to loss = 90 × 0.2333 = 20.97 crores i.e. 21 crores.

questions.question: Insurance is a __________ group.
questions.explanation: Insurance is a part of our lives. We insure our cars, our lives, and we insure our health. In insurance if a person meets with a loss, the insurance companies compensate the loss. Thus insurance is a loss sharing mechanism.

questions.question: __________ is not relevant to ascertain the machine value.
questions.explanation: When determining the value of a machine, relevant factors include: Number of shifts (affects wear and tear), Working environment (influences depreciation and maintenance), Make (determines brand value and reliability), Age (impacts depreciation and residual value). However, colour has no bearing on the machine's functional or economic value.

questions.question: Identify the reasons as to why insurance should pool homogeneous risks.
options: To predict loss probability in a better way
To ensure increased efficiency in the marketing force
To make better use of Technology
questions.correctAnswer: To predict loss probability in a better way
questions.explanation: If different heterogeneous risks are grouped together it could result in adverse selection. Only homogeneous risks that have similar exposures are pooled together so that their loss probability could be more accurately measured.

questions.question: Tort is required to ensure__________.
options: that motor vehicles do not meet with accidents
questions.explanation: Tort is a civil wrong. Each person owes a duty of care to others. The duty of care is to conduct one's activities in such a manner as to not cause injury to another person or damage to another person's property. Thus Subrogation arises under Tort.

questions.question: __________ is not possible in a speculative risk.
questions.explanation: The most important aspect of a Speculative Risk is that it is undertaken voluntarily. Speculative Risks cause losses, only when you venture to undertake a Speculative activity. Speculative Risks could result in three possible outcomes: Profit, Loss and No Profit No Loss. Therefore, 'Only loss' is not possible — profit is also possible.

questions.question: Surveyors have to be appointed within __________.
options: 72 hours of admission to the hospital
questions.explanation: In a majority of the claims, the Licensed Surveyor is the person who assesses the quantum of loss. As soon as an intimation of a loss is received, the Insurer appoints a Surveyor to assess the loss. The Insurer should appoint the Surveyor within 72 hours of the loss intimation.

questions.question: Which of the following is not true?
options: Quota Share is a Proportional Reinsurance arrangement
Stop Loss is a Proportional Reinsurance arrangement
Excess of Loss could be reinsured either facultatively or by treaty
Surplus is a Proportional Reinsurance arrangement
questions.correctAnswer: Stop Loss is a Proportional Reinsurance arrangement
questions.explanation: Stop Loss is a Non-Proportional Reinsurance arrangement.

questions.question: Which of the following Acts does not deal with Liability?
questions.explanation: Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 does not deal with Liability.

questions.question: Which of the following events is not an Insured Event?
questions.explanation: Change in Fashion is not a Pure Risk but a Speculative Risk. A Speculative Risk could result in a Profit or Loss, and not insurable.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a homogeneous group of risks?
options: A group of people of different ages
A group of cars used as taxis
A group of containers containing textile goods
A group of students in Class X
questions.correctAnswer: A group of people of different ages
questions.explanation: A group of people belonging to different ages is a heterogeneous group.

questions.question: Stability means?
questions.explanation: Stability means being steady. An enterprise should record consistent results to satisfy the needs of the investors. Insurance insulates the enterprise from volatilities caused by unforeseen losses.

questions.question: Which of the following is not relevant to decide admissibility of a claim?
questions.explanation: First, admissibility of the claim is decided, once it is decided that the claim is payable, sum Insured is relevant for effecting payment. Hence Sum Insured is not relevant for deciding admissibility.

questions.question: Which of the following might not result in a catastrophic loss?
options: A small factory located in a remote area
questions.correctAnswer: A small factory located in a remote area
questions.explanation: A small factory located in a remote area might not result in a catastrophe.

questions.question: What will be the result if more business is secured by charging less than the applicable premium?
questions.explanation: Unviable Pricing will increase the loss.

questions.question: Which concept seeks to account all expenses relating to the financial year?
questions.explanation: Accrual Concept is for recording of all transactions occurring during a particular period, even if the monetary value of these transactions could take place in the Succeeding year. The Accrual Concept ensures that all transactions occurring during that year are accounted in the same year, regardless of when the payment is made or income is received.

questions.question: A material fact means:
options: Information about the material used in the risk
Facts which are in public domain
Facts which enable an Insurer to decide whether to accept a risk or not
Facts which enable an Insurer to understand what competition is doing
questions.correctAnswer: Facts which enable an Insurer to decide whether to accept a risk or not
questions.explanation: Material facts are those that enable an Insurer to decide whether to accept a risk or not, and if accepting, on what rates and terms.

questions.question:
Following is the loss register of ABC Company for the residences covered in the year 2021-22. What is the severity?
Date of Loss | Amount
02-04-2021 | 1,71,000
08-06-2021 | 12,00,000
05-08-2021 | 4,50,000
26-08-2021 | 67,000
22-11-2021 | 43,000
05-01-2022 | 70,00,000
11-01-2022 | 1,69,000
__________ as a peril is not applicable to an automobile.
questions.explanation: Illness is not a peril applicable to an automobile, as it refers to a condition affecting living beings, not vehicles. On the other hand, perils such as accident, fire, theft, and collision are directly relevant to automobiles and are commonly covered under motor insurance policies.

questions.question: Other than claims for events occurring during the current year, identify the claim payments that are made during the current year.
options: Claims for events that will never occur
Claims for events that will occur in future
Claims for events that have occurred in the previous year
questions.correctAnswer: Claims for events that have occurred in the previous year
questions.explanation: In addition to claims arising from events during the current year, insurers may also make payments for claims related to events that occurred in the previous year. These claims might still be under processing or resolution due to the time required for verification, documentation, and settlement.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Under-insurance?
options: To make sure that the customer makes premium payment commensurate with the exposure
To make sure that the customer reduces the loss
To make sure that the customer gets lesser amount
questions.correctAnswer: To make sure that the customer makes premium payment commensurate with the exposure
questions.explanation: Underinsurance is an important concept designed to ensure that the Insured customer pays the premium for the complete exposure. Underinsurance is also known as the Condition of Average.

questions.question: The Net Incurred claims is __________ assuming incurred claims on direct business is Rs.9,500 cr., incurred claims on Reinsurance accepted is Rs.400 cr., incurred claims on Reinsurance ceded is Rs.3,600 cr.
questions.explanation: Net Incurred Claims = Incurred Claims on Direct Business + Incurred Claims on Reinsurance Accepted - Incurred Claims on Reinsurance Ceded = 9500 + 400 - 3600 = 6300.

questions.question: Identify the statement that is correct.
options: Physical laws work in different ways for different scales
Physical laws are accurate only for small volumes
Physical laws are the same for large and small volumes
Physical laws are accurate only for large volumes
Physical laws are inaccurate for all volumes
questions.correctAnswer: Physical laws are the same for large and small volumes
questions.explanation: Physical laws are reliable across geographies, across situations, across time. The Law of Large Numbers is not a physical law; it is a statistical law. Physical laws are universal. The law works in the same way at a small scale or at a large scale.

questions.question: Too much dependency on Quota share reinsurance could lead to __________.
questions.explanation: The Insurer should avoid dependence on Quota Share in the long run, as they would be ceding profitable business to the Reinsurer instead of realising the profits to their own account.

questions.question: Hazard is considered a condition due to which the probability of the loss increases or ______.
questions.explanation: Even for the same Peril and the same type of Risk, probability of loss varies depending on some features. These features that increase the probability of loss, and increase the amount of loss, are called Hazards.

questions.question: __________ is not relevant to assess the value of human life.
questions.explanation: Insurers have devised methods to calculate human life value depending on age, income, occupation and financial standing. Marital status is not one of the relevant factors used to assess the value of human life.

questions.question: Identify the correct formula for calculating the Net Premium.
options: Gross Direct Premium + Reserve for Unearned Premium for the previous year - Reserve for Unearned Premium for the current year
Gross Direct Premium – Reserve for Unearned Premium
Gross Direct Premium + Reinsurance Premium accepted
Gross Direct Premium + Reinsurance Premium accepted – Reinsurance premium ceded
questions.correctAnswer: Gross Direct Premium + Reinsurance Premium accepted – Reinsurance premium ceded
questions.explanation: Net Premium is computed as under: Gross Direct Premium + Reinsurance Premium Accepted - Reinsurance Premium Ceded.

questions.question: In a void contract, __________ can enforce it.
options: the party to whom the misrepresentation was made
the party who made the misrepresentation
questions.explanation: A void contract means it is not legally enforceable. Neither party to the contract can choose to enforce it. It is no contract at all.

questions.question:
What is the Ultimate claims cost, considering the data given below?
Claims cost 9500 crores
Survey fee and advocate fee 500 crores
Recovery from reinsurers 2000 crores
Recovery from carriers 200 crores
questions.explanation: Ultimate Claims Cost = (Claims Cost + Associated Expenses) – (Recoveries) = (9500+500) – (2000+200) = 10,000 – 2,200 = Rs.7,800 crores.

questions.question: Given, the Sum Insured is 50 crores and the Value at risk is 30 crores with the loss being 15 crores, calculate the loss payable.
questions.explanation: Sum Insured = Rs.50 crores, Value at Risk (Actual Value of Property) = Rs.30 crores, Loss Amount = Rs.15 crores. Since Sum Insured (Rs.50 Cr) is more than the Value at Risk (Rs.30 Cr), there is over insurance, not underinsurance. No application of average clause when Sum Insured ≥ Value at Risk. Since the full loss (Rs.15 Cr) is within both the Sum Insured and Value at Risk, the insurer will pay the entire admissible loss.

questions.question: Reinsurance commission is a payment as compensation for commission __________.
options: on direct business and cost of administering the policies
questions.correctAnswer: on direct business and cost of administering the policies
questions.explanation: Reinsurance commission is a payment made by the reinsurer to the ceding company (insurer) as a form of compensation. It covers: the commission the insurer paid to its agents or brokers for acquiring the original (direct) business, and the administrative costs involved in underwriting and servicing those policies.

questions.question: Kartik makes a misrepresentation to Paresh and on basis of this misrepresentation, the contract is concluded. In this case, __________ can declare the contract invalid.
questions.explanation: In contract law, misrepresentation refers to a false statement of fact made by one party (here, Kartik) that induces the other party (Paresh) to enter into a contract. Since Paresh was misled by Kartik's misrepresentation, he has the right to rescind (declare invalid) the contract. In this case, only Paresh can declare the contract invalid.

questions.question: Identify the feature that distinguishes a speculative risk from a pure risk.
questions.explanation: Risks could be grouped into two types: Pure Risks and Speculative Risks. Pure Risks are those that cause a loss, and never a gain. In all these situations, there are only two possible outcomes: Loss or No Loss. Speculative Risks could result in three possible outcomes: Profit, Loss, No Profit No Loss. Thus, Profit is the distinguishing feature.

questions.question: __________ is not a principle of insurance.
questions.explanation: Principles of Insurance are: Utmost Good Faith, Insurable Interest, Indemnity, Subrogation, Contribution, Proximate Cause. Profitability is not a principle of insurance.

questions.question: Identify the policies in which Contribution will apply.
questions.explanation: Contribution applies wherever there is more than one Policy indemnifying the loss. Two or more Policies of Indemnity exist; Contribution would apply only when the concerned Policies are Indemnity Policies. Fire policies are indemnity policies, so contribution applies to 2 fire policies.

questions.question: Formula for calculating the Loss Payable in case of underinsurance is __________.
options: Admissible Loss * Value at risk / Sum insured
Admissible Loss * Sum insured / Value at risk
questions.correctAnswer: Admissible Loss * Sum insured / Value at risk
questions.explanation: In any claim, if the Sum Insured is less than the value at risk, there is underinsurance. The amount payable after underinsurance could be calculated by the formula: Amount Payable after Underinsurance = Loss Assessed × Sum Insured / Value at Risk.
